clips.text_en_b1: In one week's time you will know why you held XRP, BTC and DOGE through the toughest five years any investor has ever faced. Five years of holding through pain, and the payoff is supposedly coming next week. Hodlers are posting this as a victory lap setup.

signal.rationale: OP implicitly bullish on holding BTC/XRP/DOGE through 5-year drawdown, expecting breakout next week

clips.text_en_b2: In roughly one week's time, investors will supposedly find out why holding XRP, BTC and DOGE through the most brutal five-year stretch any crypto holder has endured was worth the pain. The original poster frames this as a vindication moment, suggesting the patience will finally pay off. After half a decade of relentless drawdowns, the implication is clear: those who managed to hold on are about to be proven right.
clips.text_en_c1: Within a single week, the rationale for enduring what can only be described as the most punishing five-year stretch any retail investor has weathered will finally become apparent. Those who refused to capitulate on XRP, BTC, and DOGE, absorbing drawdown after drawdown with grim determination, are now positioning themselves for a vindication narrative. What began as quiet conviction has morphed into a coordinated victory lap, with hodlers across forums posting the same prophetic template. Should the anticipated move materialise, the suffering will retrospectively be reframed as tuition paid in advance. Whether markets oblige remains, of course, an entirely separate matter.
clips.text_en_c2: A self-styled crypto evangelist is publicly proclaiming that within a single trading week, the rationale behind enduring XRP, BTC, and DOGE through what he describes as the most punishing five-year stretch any market participant has ever weathered will become manifestly vindicated. Five years of unflagging conviction through successive drawdowns, sustained ostensibly on faith alone, are now being positioned as the prelude to imminent vindication. The post reads less as analysis than as ritualistic affirmation, the kind of declaration one issues before a long-anticipated payoff materialises, or fails to. Hodlers circulate the message as a victory lap already rehearsed, a preemptive coronation of a thesis whose merit remains, for now, a matter of doctrinal belief rather than demonstrated return.

clips.text_zh: Warsh同Bessent搞咩鬼呀？Powell又俾Trump鬧，通脹又唔理，搞個taskforce扮嘢。wtf 美國儲局真係黐線，gold同oil睇緊。
clips.text_en_b1: The Federal Reserve is NOT going to hike. Warsh creates a taskforce but does nothing. Bessent wants to buy yen and hints at dumping a trillion in buybacks. Trump criticizes Powell for not cutting rates because the economy is so good it deserves lower rates. The setup is dovish.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about the Fed not hiking, Warsh/Bessent doing nothing

signal.rationale: Dovish Fed narrative is bullish for gold as real yields drop

clips.text_en_b2: The Federal Reserve is unlikely to hike rates anytime soon, despite the theatre surrounding it. While Warsh has quietly set up a taskforce that does little of substance, Bessent has been hinting at intervention through yen purchases and a potential trillion-dollar buyback scheme. Meanwhile, Trump keeps pressuring Powell to cut rates on the grounds that the economy is thriving. The overall picture leans dovish, which has gold and oil watchers paying close attention.
clips.text_en_c1: The Federal Reserve, in its current configuration, is highly unlikely to proceed with any rate hike whatsoever. Kevin Warsh has conspicuously established a taskforce whose remit appears confined to issuing press releases rather than enacting policy, while Scott Bessent has floated the rather extraordinary notion of intervening in yen markets and orchestrating a trillion-dollar buyback operation. Meanwhile, the President has once again taken to publicly admonishing Chair Powell, arguing that an economy performing as robustly as this one ostensibly deserves materially lower borrowing costs. Against this backdrop, the macroeconomic setup remains distinctly dovish, which is why gold and crude have been bid accordingly.
clips.text_en_c2: The conviction that the Federal Reserve will refrain from hiking rates is hardening among market commentators, notwithstanding the labyrinthine theatre surrounding the institution. Warsh has convened a taskforce that has thus far produced nothing of substance; Bessent, for his part, is openly agitating for yen intervention while floating the prospect of deploying roughly a trillion dollars into corporate buybacks, a staggering figure whose plausibility remains questionable. Trump, meanwhile, has resumed his customary broadsides against Powell, lambasting the Chair for declining to cut rates on the dubious premise that economic strength itself warrants accommodation. The cumulative effect is decidedly dovish positioning, which is precisely why gold and crude are being watched with such wary attentiveness.

clips.text_zh: X Corp又嚟搞Nitter啦，抄人Texas法ban咗十幾個instance，轉個頭另一啲又即刻出返嚟。FOSS真係打不死，lol。
clips.text_en_b1: Nitter is back online. X Corp sent a cease and desist letter to the FOSS front-end project, citing the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act. They went after individual instances and even unrelated embed sites. They all complied. Within days, a dozen alternate instances popped up elsewhere.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread about X Corp killing Nitter frontends and new ones spawning

signal.rationale: Tech/AI observation clip, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Nitter has come back online after X Corp's latest crackdown. According to reports, the company issued cease and desist letters to the FOSS front-end project, invoking the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act. They pursued individual instances and even unrelated embed sites, all of which complied. Within days, however, roughly a dozen alternative instances had already sprung up elsewhere, proving once again that open-source projects have a way of bouncing back.
clips.text_en_c1: Nitter, the privacy-preserving FOSS front-end for X, has resurfaced after a brief but concerted campaign of legal intimidation. X Corp dispatched a cease and desist invoking the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act, a statute whose applicability to public-content aggregation remains contested. Not content with targeting the primary instances, their legal team also pursued unrelated embed services, all of which complied promptly. Yet within mere days, a dozen alternative mirrors had already materialised elsewhere, demonstrating once again that genuinely decentralised infrastructure tends to recover faster than it can be suppressed. The cat-and-mouse dynamic, it seems, is firmly back on.
clips.text_en_c2: Nitter, the FOSS front-end that long served as the principal refuge for users seeking to view X content without the indignity of authentication or tracking, has resurfaced after a concerted legal offensive. X Corp dispatched cease and desist correspondence invoking the Texas Harmful Access by Computer Act, a statute whose applicability to open-source scraping remains contested. The campaign systematically targeted individual instances and, in a notably aggressive flourish, even ancillary embed sites, all of whom capitulated promptly. Yet within a matter of days, a fresh constellation of approximately a dozen mirror instances has materialised elsewhere, hosted by developers who evidently regard the legal threat as an occupational hazard rather than a deterrent. The whack-a-mole dynamic persists.

clips.text_en_b2: A /pol/ rant argues that white people increasingly resent Indians precisely because India refused to become subservient to the West. The poster claims the West only seems to admire ethnicities that stay comfortably obedient. India, once romanticised by hippies as a spiritual haven, has undergone a dramatic shift in perception as its global influence has grown. The thread descends into classic ethnic geopolitics, blaming shifting attitudes on India's rising stature.
clips.text_en_c1: A lengthy geopolitical screed on /pol/ argues that Western sentiment toward India has curdled precisely because the subcontinent declined to occupy the subservient role historically expected of non-European civilisations. The poster contends that prior affection, manifested in the hippy trail era when India functioned as a spiritual playground for disaffected Western youth, has given way to resentment now that New Delhi wields genuine diplomatic and economic leverage. Ethnic relations, in this framing, function as a barometer of geopolitical obedience; populations that refuse deference invariably attract contempt. Returning to LIHKG afterwards felt, by contrast, like a return to relative sanity.
clips.text_en_c2: A polemic circulating on /pol/ contends that Western antipathy toward Indians stems not from cultural friction but from a recalibration of historical deference, the assertion being that the Anglosphere only genuinely esteems those populations content to remain perpetually subordinate. The poster frames India's refusal of historical servility as the proximate cause of contemporary resentment, arguing that the subcontinent's emergence as a geopolitical heavyweight has irrevocably altered the calculus of Western affection. There is, admittedly, a certain grim irony in observing that India was once venerated as a spiritual Mecca for disaffected Western youth, a locus of mystical import, whereas it is now regarded with suspicion precisely because it possesses the material capacity to defy external pressure.

clips.text_en_b2: Does anyone else find it genuinely suspicious that the developer behind this new Nintendo project isn't credited anywhere in the trailer, the official website, or any promotional materials whatsoever? The original poster wondered openly which studio Nintendo had outsourced the work to. While speculation ranges from a hidden first-party team to potential AI involvement, the conspicuous absence of any studio logo remains a glaring oddity.
clips.text_en_c1: Is nobody remotely bothered by the conspicuous absence of any credited developer across the entire promotional apparatus for this supposed Nintendo release? The trailer, the official site, the press kit, and every ancillary marketing channel omit even a studio logo, which would be unthinkable for a genuine first-party production. The implication, whether intentional or otherwise, is that the project has been outsourced to an external partner whose identity Nintendo evidently wishes to withhold. Whether this reflects an unannounced collaboration with an established studio, a smaller indie outfit, or something altogether more speculative remains the question exercising the commentariat.
clips.text_en_c2: The conspicuous absence of any credited developer in Nintendo's newly unveiled trailer, official website, and associated promotional apparatus has not escaped the more paranoid elements of the gaming community, who regard such omission as categorically anomalous for a project that otherwise bears every superficial hallmark of a first-party release. The studio's name, ordinarily a fixture of any self-respecting Nintendo marketing campaign, is nowhere to be found, prompting speculation that the work has been outsourced to an external contractor whose identity Nintendo is either disinclined or contractually prohibited from disclosing. Whether this represents standard operational secrecy or something more disquieting, perhaps the increasingly ubiquitous deployment of generative AI tools in game production, remains a matter of conjecture.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信一定笑我，仲未上到1pl8 OHP reps。但squat同DL都過哂，OHP真係最廢。繼續grind，gym唔等人。💪
clips.text_en_b1: I'm closer to a 1-plate overhead press than I am to a 2-plate bench, 3-plate squat, or 4-plate deadlift. The poster thinks a 1-plate OHP for reps is realistic in one or two months. Upper-body pressing is clearly lagging compared to lower-body lifts.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about lifting progression, specifically OHP

signal.rationale: Fitness observation clip, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: I've managed to clear a three-plate squat and a four-plate deadlift, yet a proper one-plate overhead press for reps still eludes me. The frustrating reality is that my pressing strength lags considerably behind my lower-body lifts, so a one-plate OHP within a couple of months feels like a realistic goal. Meanwhile, a two-plate bench remains stubbornly out of reach. The grind continues regardless.
clips.text_en_c1: Although my squat has comfortably cleared the three-plate threshold and my deadlift has breached four plates with relative consistency, my overhead press stubbornly refuses to cooperate, lagging behind to such an extent that achieving a single plate for multiple repetitions still represents an aspirational rather than accomplished milestone. The disparity between my lower-body development and pressing strength has become almost comical, a familiar affliction among lifters whose legs respond readily to progressive overload while their shoulders remain obstinately recalcitrant. Two months of focused pressing work should, in theory, remedy the situation, provided I resist the temptation to neglect accessories.
clips.text_en_c2: A frustratingly lopsided progression has befallen the poster's lifting portfolio: he stands tantalisingly closer to a one-plate overhead press for reps than to any of the more celebrated milestones in conventional strength training nomenclature, the two-plate bench, the three-plate squat, or the four-plate deadlift, all of which remain comfortably within reach while the comparatively modest OHP target continues to elude him. He estimates, with the cautious optimism characteristic of intermediates, that a one-plate overhead for clean reps is achievable within perhaps two months of dedicated training. The diagnosis is unmistakable: his posterior chain and lower-body mechanics have developed apace, whereas his pressing strength, a stubborn deficiency afflicting lifters with longer torsos, lags conspicuously behind.

clips.text_en_c2: Weekly Shonen Magazine's forty-first issue for 2026 has arrived bearing its customary cargo of serialised content, prominently featuring colour pages for Yowayowa, an established title, alongside a fresh new series entitled Onryou Biyori, whose thematic orientation remains, for the moment, an exercise in informed speculation. The publisher's strategy of rotating prospective titles on a roughly quarterly basis, a deliberate mechanism for gauging market reception before committing to longer runs, continues to characterise the magazine's editorial philosophy.
